Usage: gwt <command>
   or: gwt <branch> [<base>] [flags]

gwt creates and removes Git worktrees under one placement policy, and judges whether branches are merged into the trunk.

A branch's worktree lives at <worktree_root>/<name of the main checkout>/<branch>.
Git owns repository state; gwt owns where checkouts go, what is copied into them,
and when one may be removed. Create and remove worktrees through gwt rather than
git worktree, so every checkout follows the same placement and removal rules.

The first word is the command; anything else there is a branch for create, so
"gwt feat/x main" creates feat/x from main. To create a branch named like a
command, write "gwt create list".

stdout carries only the result: a path, one line per item, or with --json one JSON
document (remove prints one JSON object per line, one per target). Progress,
warnings and the confirmation prompt go to stderr. gwt never changes the caller's
directory; agents use the printed path as their working directory.

Flags:
  -h, --help               Show context-sensitive help.

Arguments and flags of create, the default command:
  <branch>                 The branch to check out; created when no local or remote branch has the
                           name.
  <base>                   Where a new branch forks from; unused when a local branch or one remote
                           branch has the name. Default: the configured base (optional).
  -n, --non-interactive    Fork a new branch from the configured base without asking, even when that
                           base is HEAD. Agents and scripts pass this.
      --new                Create a new branch even when a remote branch has the name; an existing
                           local branch is still checked out as it is.
      --no-copy            Copy no ignored files from the main checkout into the new one.
      --no-clipboard       Leave the clipboard alone at a terminal.
      --no-fetch           Decide from cached remote refs, without fetching.
      --cd                 Enter the new checkout in the calling shell. Only the zsh gwt function
                           from dotfiles can, so the binary refuses this flag.
      --json               Print one JSON object instead of the path.

Commands:
  create <branch> [<base>]    Check out a branch in its own worktree, creating the branch if needed,
                              and print the path (default).
  resolve <branch>            Say how create would obtain a branch: local, remote, ambiguous or
                              absent.
  path [<branch>]             Print where create would place a branch, without creating anything.
  remove <target> ...         Remove checkouts and their branches, keeping a recovery ref for
                              anything discarded.
  list                        List every worktree with its changes and whether its branch is merged
                              into the trunk.
  merged <target> ...         Judge whether branches or commits are merged into the trunk.
  trunk                       Print the trunk: the branch work lands on, which merge verdicts
                              measure against.
  config show                 Print the effective configuration and the file each value came from.

Exit codes:
  0    success
  1    failed, or a creation was declined; also remove when any target failed, and merged when any
       target could not be judged, after printing every target's result
  2    invalid arguments; nothing was run

Run "gwt <command> --help" for a command's details.
